video.transcriptSummary: This course is a living meta-build reference model: every single stage you study is backed by the real markdown specs, ADRs, hooks, skills, and code that built Antigravity Academy itself. Starting from Stage 1 (cf-research), you see how dependency auditing caught GSAP's proprietary EULA before a single package was installed. In Stages 2 and 3 (cf-grill-me + cf-plan), five crisp questions locked our isolated Next.js App Router architecture in ADR-0002 and froze Zod schemas in plans/antigravity-academy-spec.md. In Stage 4 (cf-implement), Task 0 froze shared interfaces so four parallel Swarm workers built the Backend APIs, Three.js 3D Engine, Glassmorphic UI, and Vitest suite without a single overlapping file edit. In Stages 5 and 6 (cf-qa-review + cf-deploy-staging), an independent cf-reviewer audited security boundaries while the browser subagent verified 375px, 768px, and 1440px viewports prior to a HITL-gated Vercel preview deploy. Finally, Stages 7 and 8 (cf-triage + cf-learn + cf-handover) show how to convert lessons into permanent rules and add Course N+1 in any future conversation.

steps.title: Stage 1 — Research: Discovery, Trade-Offs & License Auditing
steps.summary: Never jump straight into coding. Stage 1 (`cf-research` via `cf-architect`) inspects the workspace, evaluates architectural options, audits dependency licenses (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD), and flags upfront security risks in `.memory/research*.md`.
keyTakeaways: Live Meta-Build Win: During Stage 1 of Antigravity Academy, dependency inspection flagged GSAP's proprietary Webflow Standard License and immediately replaced it with MIT-licensed `motion` before any code was written.

Plugin Root Isolation constraint discovered early: because the repo root is symlinked into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/code-factory`, the web platform had to live inside `academy/` to keep plugin discovery spotless.
Every research doc ends with a human Senior Engineer Sign-Off Gate confirming trade-offs, licenses, and security posture.
actionChecklist: Open `.memory/research-academy-platform.md` in the Repo Explorer to inspect the full dependency compliance table.
Verify every new package has a permissive license (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/ISC) and zero known High/Critical CVEs.
Require explicit human sign-off on architectural trade-offs before opening Stage 2.
steps.mermaidDiagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Idea / Goal"] --> B["cf-research (Codebase + Tooling Audit)"]
    B --> C["License & CVE Gate (Reject GSAP -> Pick MIT Motion)"]
    C --> D[".memory/research.md"]
    D --> E{"Senior Engineer Sign-Off"}

steps.title: Stage 2 — Spec: Interrogating Ambiguity & Locking Contracts
steps.summary: Ambiguous requirements cause expensive rework. Stage 2 pairs `cf-grill-me` (up to 5 sharp decision questions) with `cf-plan` to freeze a self-contained specification at `plans/<feature>-spec.md` with Zod schemas, error envelopes, and explicit non-goals.
keyTakeaways: Live Meta-Build Win: `cf-grill-me` locked 5 decisive calls in under two minutes—Next.js App Router over raw HTML, stateless v1 `localStorage` + Zod, dark glassmorphic palette, unified `VideoStage`, and pure TypeScript HITL simulation.
Every API endpoint specifies its exact Zod schema, pagination defaults (`limit=20`, `max=100`), Vercel `maxDuration`, and 4xx/5xx error codes before implementation begins.
Explicit Non-Goals prevent scope creep during Swarm execution (e.g., deferring Supabase Auth + Postgres RLS cleanly to v2).
actionChecklist: Inspect `plans/antigravity-academy-spec.md` in the Repo Explorer to see how Zod contracts and UI state matrices are specified.
Never skip `cf-grill-me` when a request leaves persistence, auth, or visual direction ambiguous.
Verify the locked spec lists explicit Loading, Error, Empty, and WCAG 2.1 AA states for every interactive component.

steps.title: Stage 3 — Architecture: System Maps, ADRs & Design Tokens
steps.summary: Durable decisions belong in `.memory/decisions/` (ADRs) and `.memory/architecture.md`, not buried in ephemeral chat history. Stage 3 freezes boundaries, rejected alternatives, Tailwind v4 `@theme` design tokens, and non-overlapping file partitions.
keyTakeaways: Live Meta-Build Win: `ADR-0002` explicitly documents why direct imperative Three.js islands beat `@react-three/fiber` (zero React 19 peer friction + full WebGL/DPR/IntersectionObserver control) and why build-time allowlisted repo sync prevents secret leaks.
Design System Invariant: All colors, typography (`Space Grotesk` + `JetBrains Mono`), and glass surfaces live in `globals.css` `@theme` tokens—zero hardcoded hex values in UI components.
Partition Planning: Decomposing the work into Task 0 (shared schemas/tokens) + Tasks 1–4 guarantees parallel agents never overwrite each other's files.
actionChecklist: Read `.memory/decisions/0002-academy-nextjs-glassmorphic-architecture.md` in the Repo Explorer.
Check that every ADR records Context, Decision, Alternatives Considered, and Consequences.
Confirm Task 0 freezes all shared TypeScript interfaces (`schemas.ts`, `contracts.ts`) before launching parallel builders.
steps.mermaidDiagram:
flowchart TD
    T0["Task 0: Shared Schemas, Contracts & Design Tokens"] --> T1["Task 1: Backend APIs, HITL Evaluator & Course JSON"]
    T0 --> T2["Task 2: Three.js 3D Engine Islands"]
    T0 --> T3["Task 3: Glassmorphic UI Components"]
    T0 --> T4["Task 4: Deterministic Vitest Suite"]
    T1 --> QA["Stage 5: Independent QA & Browser Audit"]
    T2 --> QA

steps.title: Stage 4 — Build: Task 0 Lock & Non-Overlapping Swarm Execution
steps.summary: Execution (`cf-implement`) strictly follows the locked spec. The orchestrator completes Task 0 first, then fans out clean `cf-backend` and `cf-frontend` workers onto strictly non-overlapping file partitions—preventing context rot and merge conflicts.
keyTakeaways: Separation of Concerns: The architect who writes the spec is decoupled from the builders implementing it, and builders never invent unapproved dependencies or routes.
Zero File Contention: Task 1 owns `scripts/`, `content/`, `src/lib/`, `src/data/`, and `src/app/api/`; Task 2 owns `src/components/three/`; Task 3 owns UI components; Task 4 owns `tests/`.
All business logic ships with strict TypeScript (zero `any`), runtime Zod validation, and deterministic pure functions (zero `child_process` in API routes).
actionChecklist: Inspect `skills/cf-implement/references/orchestration.md` to review the exact Swarm partitioning rules.
Run `pnpm run sync:resources` to verify the allowlisted build-time manifest regenerates cleanly with zero errors.
Verify local `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` before handing off to Stage 5 QA.

steps.title: Stage 5 — Test: Independent Security Review & 3-Viewport Browser QA
steps.summary: Never let the author grade their own homework. Stage 5 (`cf-qa-review`) invokes `cf-reviewer` in a clean read-only context to audit the diff against `rules/AGENTS.md`, while the built-in `browser` subagent visually verifies 375px, 768px, and 1440px viewports.
keyTakeaways: 4-Layer Verification Gate: (1) Static checks (`tsc`, `eslint`, `next build`), (2) Deterministic Vitest parity & component suite, (3) Independent `cf-reviewer` SAST/invariant diff audit, (4) Live `browser` visual + console audit.

Visual Evidence Standard: The browser subagent validates layout stability (zero CLS), glassmorphism contrast (>= 4.5:1), keyboard focus rings, and zero console/hydration errors at Mobile (375px), Tablet (768px), and Desktop (1440px).
Output is persisted to `.memory/qa-report.md`—Stage 6 Deploy is strictly blocked if any P0/P1 defect remains.
actionChecklist: Inspect `agents/cf-reviewer.md` and `skills/cf-qa-review/SKILL.md` in the Repo Explorer.
Verify all 4 Vitest suites pass deterministically with zero flaky timers or network mocks leaking.
Confirm `.memory/qa-report.md` records explicit Pass clearance across security, tests, and all 3 responsive viewports.

steps.title: Stage 6 — Deploy: Rollback Plan, HITL Approval & Preview Smoke Tests
steps.summary: Remote deployments are high-impact actions gated by both `cf-deploy-staging` and `hooks/hitl-gate.py`. Before pushing to Vercel Staging, the agent verifies QA clearance, documents the exact rollback command, obtains explicit human approval, and runs post-deploy smoke tests.
keyTakeaways: Human-in-the-Loop Gate: `hooks/hitl-gate.py` enforces `force_ask` on `vercel --prod`, `wrangler deploy`, `supabase db push`, and `git push`, while permitting read-only `--dry-run` checks.
Rollback-First Discipline: Document the exact `vercel rollback <deployment-url>` command in `.memory/handover.md` *before* triggering a deployment.
Post-Deploy Smoke Test: Validate live HTTP 200 on `/`, `/api/courses`, `/api/resources`, and `POST /api/hitl/simulate` on the deployed staging preview URL.
actionChecklist: Verify `.memory/qa-report.md` contains zero blocking defects before requesting staging deploy approval.
Test `vercel deploy` (staging preview) vs. `vercel --prod` (force_ask) in the live HITL Gate Simulator.
Record the staging preview URL, rollback command, and smoke-test results in `.memory/handover.md`.

codeSnippet.code:
# 1. Deploy staging preview (after human approval)
cd academy && vercel deploy

# 2. Smoke-test live API contracts (<= 5000ms timeout invariant)
curl --max-time 5 -sf "$STAGING_URL/api/courses?limit=5" | jq '.total'
curl --max-time 5 -sf "$STAGING_URL/api/resources?category=skill&limit=20" | jq '.total'
curl --max-time 5 -sf -X POST "$STAGING_URL/api/hitl/simulate" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"commandLine":"git push --force"}' | jq '.decision'

steps.title: Stage 7 — User Feedback: Structured Triage & Severity Backlog
steps.summary: Real learners and staging telemetry always surface edge cases that unit tests miss. Stage 7 (`cf-triage`) classifies feedback and runtime logs by severity (P0–P3), isolates root causes, and queues actionable items in `.memory/tasks.md`.
keyTakeaways: Structured Triage beats ad-hoc patching: every bug report or UX friction point receives a severity tier (P0 Critical, P1 High, P2 Medium, P3 Enhancement) and minimal reproduction steps.
Separate quick regression fixes from new features: P0/P1 bugs enter immediate remediation while new course requests queue cleanly into the multi-course backlog.
Every staging observation links directly back to affected files, API endpoints, and viewport dimensions.
actionChecklist: Inspect `skills/cf-triage/SKILL.md` and `.memory/tasks.md` to see how active backlog items are tracked.
Log every staging UX observation with its exact viewport width, reproduction step, and expected vs. actual behavior.
Prioritize P0/P1 regressions ahead of new feature work.

steps.title: Stage 8 — Optimise: Distill Invariants, Handover & Add Course N+1
steps.summary: Every completed cycle should make the factory permanently smarter. Stage 8 pairs `cf-learn` (promoting bug post-mortems into permanent rules & regression tests) with `cf-handover` (writing a <= 3 KB `.memory/handover.md`) so the next conversation starts hot and can drop in Course N+1 cleanly.
keyTakeaways: Permanent Learning (`cf-learn`): Whenever a subtle bug is resolved (like GSAP's license or `PreToolUse` failing closed on `{}`), codify the invariant in `.agents/rules/` + a regression test so it can never recur.
Context Hygiene (`cf-handover`): Keep `.memory/handover.md` strictly <= 3 KB with current git status, completed milestones, and the exact next action for instant cross-model resumption.

Infinite Course Extensibility: Any future conversation in this repo can drop a new Zod-validated `academy/content/courses/<slug>/course.json` and run `pnpm run sync:resources`—the UI, Prompt Vault, and `/api/courses` update automatically!
actionChecklist: Inspect `skills/cf-learn/SKILL.md`, `skills/cf-handover/SKILL.md`, and `.memory/handover.md`.
Use the 'Add Course N+1' prompt below in your very next conversation to package any new project milestone into Course 3.
Export your learner progress JSON backup from the Course Studio header before switching machines.
steps.mermaidDiagram:
flowchart LR
    L["Resolved Bug / Milestone"] --> R["cf-learn -> Permanent Rule + Regression Test"]
    R --> H["cf-handover -> .memory/handover.md (<= 3 KB)"]
    H --> C["New Conversation -> content/courses/<slug>/course.json"]
    C --> S["pnpm run sync:resources -> Live Academy Updated"]
    S --> NEXT["Next 8-Stage SDLC Cycle"]

prompts.title: Bootstrap Code Factory & Run Stage 1 Research
prompts.description: Initializes the `.memory/` workspace structure and kicks off a disciplined Stage 1 discovery report with license and security checks.

variables.label: Problem Statement
variables.placeholder: What user problem are we solving?
variables.defaultValue: Enable live multi-user curriculum annotations with offline resilience

prompts.expectedOutcome: A complete `.memory/` workspace and a sign-off-ready `.memory/research.md` with verified licenses and explicit trade-offs.

prompts.title: Run Stage 2A Interrogation (cf-grill-me) & Lock Spec + ADR
prompts.description: Surfaces hidden ambiguities with up to 5 focused questions and freezes an implementation-ready `plans/<feature>-spec.md` plus ADR.
prompts.template:
Execute Stage 2A (`cf-grill-me`) on `{{feature_name}}` using `.memory/research.md` as input.

Ask me up to 5 high-impact questions to eliminate all ambiguity around {{ambiguity_focus}}. Once I answer, execute Stage 2B (`cf-plan`) to produce:
1. A locked specification at `plans/{{feature_slug}}-spec.md` with Zod schemas, pagination bounds, error codes, UI Loading/Error/Empty/WCAG matrices, and non-overlapping Task 0..N file partitions.
2. An Architecture Decision Record at `.memory/decisions/{{adr_filename}}`.
Do not write production code until I approve the locked spec.

variables.label: Key Ambiguity Areas
variables.defaultValue: auth boundaries, Postgres RLS policies, and offline conflict resolution

prompts.expectedOutcome: Zero unstated assumptions, a locked `plans/<slug>-spec.md`, and a durable ADR under `.memory/decisions/`.

prompts.title: Execute Stage 4 Swarm Build from a Locked Spec
prompts.description: Runs Task 0 shared interfaces first, then fans out parallel `cf-backend` and `cf-frontend` workers onto non-overlapping file partitions.
prompts.template:
Execute Stage 3/4 (`cf-implement`) strictly from the locked specification at `{{spec_path}}`.

Execution Protocol:
1. Complete Task 0 (shared Zod schemas, contracts, and design tokens) first in the coordinator context.
2. Launch parallel workers on strictly non-overlapping file partitions (`{{worker_partitions}}`).
3. Enforce all `rules/AGENTS.md` invariants: zero hardcoded secrets, zero `any`, strict Zod validation, WCAG 2.1 AA, and deterministic unit tests.
4. Run `{{verify_cmd}}` and confirm 100% green before moving to Stage 4 QA Review.

variables.label: Parallel Worker Partitions
variables.placeholder: Task 1 Backend, Task 2 3D, Task 3 UI, Task 4 Tests
variables.defaultValue: Task 1 Backend/APIs, Task 2 3D Islands, Task 3 Glassmorphic UI, Task 4 Vitest

variables.label: Local Verification Command
variables.placeholder: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build
variables.defaultValue: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build

prompts.expectedOutcome: A complete, spec-compliant, conflict-free implementation passing typecheck, lint, unit tests, and production build.

prompts.title: Run Stage 5 Independent Security Audit & 3-Viewport Visual QA
prompts.description: Triggers `cf-reviewer` in a clean context plus the built-in `browser` subagent to audit 375px, 768px, and 1440px layouts.
prompts.template:
Execute Stage 4/5 (`cf-qa-review`) for `{{app_dir}}` served at `{{preview_url}}`:

1. Run full static checks (`tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, Vitest coverage, production build).
2. Invoke `cf-reviewer` in a clean context to inspect the diff against `rules/AGENTS.md` (security boundaries, XSS/injection, pagination, serverless timeouts, WCAG 2.1 AA).
3. Invoke the `browser` subagent to inspect `{{preview_url}}` at 375px, 768px, and 1440px—verify zero console errors, zero horizontal overflow, interactive forms, and reduced-motion safety.
4. Write the signed QA verdict to `.memory/qa-report.md`.
prompts.expectedOutcome: A thorough `.memory/qa-report.md` documenting test results, security sign-off, and multi-viewport visual verification.

prompts.title: Run Stage 6 HITL-Gated Staging Deployment & Smoke Tests
prompts.description: Verifies QA clearance, drafts the rollback plan, requests explicit human confirmation, deploys staging preview, and runs smoke checks.
prompts.template:
Execute Stage 5/6 (`cf-deploy-staging`) for `{{app_dir}}` to `{{target_platform}}` staging preview.

1. Verify `.memory/qa-report.md` shows zero blocking P0/P1 defects.
2. Document the exact rollback procedure in `.memory/handover.md` before executing any remote deploy.
3. Present the deployment plan and wait for my explicit human approval (HITL gate).
4. After approval, deploy the preview build and smoke-test `{{smoke_endpoints}}` with a <= 5000ms curl timeout.
prompts.expectedOutcome: A live staging preview URL verified by automated smoke tests and protected by a documented rollback command.

prompts.title: Run Stage 7 Staging Feedback & Incident Triage
prompts.description: Turns staging observations, user feedback, or runtime errors into severity-ranked root-cause items in `.memory/tasks.md`.
prompts.template:
Execute Stage 6A/7 (`cf-triage`) on the following staging feedback for `{{feature_name}}`:

Observed issue or learner feedback:
"{{feedback_summary}}"

1. Classify severity (P0–P3) and isolate the concrete root cause in the codebase.
2. Check whether this violates an existing invariant in `rules/AGENTS.md`.
3. Queue prioritized remediation steps in `.memory/tasks.md` with clear acceptance criteria.

variables.label: Feedback or Incident Summary
variables.placeholder: Describe the UX issue, error log, or feature request
variables.defaultValue: Learners want keyboard shortcuts to cycle through SDLC stages in the 3D Orbital viewer

prompts.expectedOutcome: Severity-ranked root-cause analysis and prioritized remediation tasks logged in `.memory/tasks.md`.

prompts.title: Stage 8 Optimise: Distill Lesson (cf-learn) & Add Course N+1
prompts.description: Promotes engineering lessons into permanent rules, updates handover.md (<= 3 KB), and scaffolds a brand-new Zod-validated Course N+1 inside Antigravity Academy.
prompts.template:
Execute Stage 6B/8 (`cf-learn` + `cf-handover`) and publish **Course {{course_number}}** into Antigravity Academy:

1. Distill the key engineering lesson from this session (`{{lesson_learned}}`) into a permanent invariant rule and regression test requirement.
2. Create `academy/content/courses/{{course_slug}}/course.json` conforming strictly to `CourseSchema` (`academy/src/lib/schemas.ts`), complete with video chapters, step-by-step walkthroughs, Mermaid diagrams, real `repoArtifactPath` links, and copyable variable prompts.
3. Run `cd academy && pnpm run sync:resources && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` to auto-ingest the new course.
4. Update `.memory/tasks.md` and write a concise <= 3 KB `.memory/handover.md`.

variables.label: Post-Mortem / Engineering Lesson
variables.placeholder: What invariant should never be violated again?
variables.defaultValue: Always validate external embed URLs and hook payloads against strict Zod allowlists

prompts.expectedOutcome: A permanent invariant rule, a fresh <= 3 KB `.memory/handover.md`, and a newly published Course N+1 live in Antigravity Academy.
